flashcards.back: Each term adds the same number (the common difference). Example: 4, 7, 10, 13 (d = 3).
Each term is multiplied by the same number (the common ratio). Example: 3, 6, 12, 24 (r = 2).

flashcards.front: A number series has no constant difference. What should you try next?
flashcards.back: Check ratios, take the differences of the differences, look for sums of previous terms, or split it into two alternating series.
E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25. Count from the nearest checkpoint.
A short sentence stating how the first pair is related, e.g., "A scalpel is a tool used by a surgeon." Test every choice with it.
Words that differ in intensity: warm : hot :: cool : cold.
"If not Q, then not P." It is always true when the original statement is true.

flashcards.front: Does "All roses are flowers" mean "All flowers are roses"?
flashcards.back: No. "All A are B" cannot be reversed into "All B are A."

flashcards.front: In a cube net, three squares are in a straight row. Which two become opposite faces?
flashcards.back: The first and third squares.
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| degrees (H = hour, M = minutes). If the result is over 180°, subtract it from 360°.
Kind and well-meaning. (bene- = good)
Lasting only a very short time.
Bad or badly. Examples: malnourished, malfunction.
Denotation is a word's dictionary meaning. Connotation is the feeling or association it carries.

flashcards.front: Neither ... nor: which subject does the verb agree with?
flashcards.back: The subject closer to the verb. "Neither the teacher nor the students ARE late."
its = belonging to it. it's = it is / it has.
Fewer for things you can count (fewer books). Less for amounts you cannot count (less water).
A logical conclusion supported by clues in the text but not directly stated.
Two independent clauses joined only by a comma. Fix with a period, a semicolon, or a comma + conjunction.
A simile compares using "like" or "as." A metaphor says one thing IS another.
x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a), for ax² + bx + c = 0.
m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁)

flashcards.front: What does the discriminant b² − 4ac tell you?
flashcards.back: Positive: two real roots. Zero: one repeated real root. Negative: no real roots.
a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent.

flashcards.front: Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon

flashcards.back: The middle value of sorted data. With an even count, average the two middle values.
I = Prt (principal × annual rate × time in years).
d/dx (xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹
The organelle where cellular respiration releases energy as ATP.
Mitosis: 2 identical body cells. Meiosis: 4 genetically different sex cells with half the chromosome number.

flashcards.front: Tt × Tt: expected ratio of traits
flashcards.back: 3 dominant : 1 recessive (genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
The number of protons in an atom's nucleus. It identifies the element.
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
Below 7: acidic. 7: neutral. Above 7: basic.
F = ma: net force equals mass times acceleration.
KE = ½mv². Doubling the speed makes KE four times larger.
V = IR (voltage = current × resistance).

flashcards.front: Why does the Philippines have many earthquakes and volcanoes?
flashcards.back: It lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where tectonic plates meet and one plate sinks beneath another.
